Q: At time of creating table in postgresql database without mentioning the schema name. What it will take name of schema? A:

That's determined by your search_path. By default it's "$user" which evaluates to a schema named the same as your user. If that doesn't exist, it'll check the next one on the search path (that's usually public) and so on. You can check it by calling current_schema():

current_schema → name
current_schema() → name
Returns the name of the schema that is first in the search path (or a null value if the search path is empty). This is the schema that will be used for any tables or other named objects that are created without specifying a target schema.

The "schema that is first in the search path" should say "first existing schema in the search path". You can have 4 entries and it'll return the 4th if the leading 3 can't be found. New objects will be created in the 4th schema: demo at db<>fiddle

drop schema if exists "1st";
drop schema if exists "2nd";
drop schema if exists "3rd";
create schema if not exists "4th";
set search_path to "1st", "2nd", "3rd", "4th";

create table my_table(i int);

select schemaname,tablename 
from pg_tables 
where tablename='my_table';
schemaname tablename
4th my_table

The "null value if the search path is empty" should actually say "null value if none of the schemas listed in your search_path exists":

set search_path to 'this_schema_does_not_exist';
select current_schema();
current_schema
null

And that obviously leads to an error:

create table my_table4(i int);

ERROR:  no schema has been selected to create in
LINE 3: create table my_table4(i int);
                     ^

Here's how you can safely add a new schema without losing sight of stuff located in whatever other schemas you had in your search path up to this point

select set_config('search_path',concat_ws(', ','your_additional_schema',current_setting('search_path')), false);

Unlike doing this:

set search_path to your_additional_schema, "$user", public;

It doesn't require you to remember or check and re-list all entries each time you change it, and unlike doing just this:

set search_path to your_additional_schema;

It doesn't remove other entries from that list, like public and "$user". Which you don't want if that's where you keep some shared functions, procedures, types that you intend to use when working on this new schema.

Q: How to can I see the allowed Whatsapp Business API solutions providers that have access to my Facebook Business? A:

If you’re trying to find something in the Facebook Business settings and can’t locate it, it might just be buried in the menu since the layout can be confusing. Try going to Business Settings → Accounts → Pages/Ad Accounts, depending on what you’re trying to manage.

If you still can’t see the option, it could also be a permissions issue, meaning your account might not have the required admin access. In that case, the business admin may need to grant you the proper role.
